subject: Suspicious batch issuance of trial credits — BrightChat accounts flagged
messages:
From: automated-fraud@redwood-inference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: [Automated] High-volume promo credit issuance — cluster detected

Hi Marissa,

Our automated abuse detector has flagged a cluster of 42 promo credit grants issued in the last 2 hours tied to the BrightChat domain and a set of Gmail addresses that match a repeating pattern (user+testXX@gmail.com). IPs originate from a narrow CIDR range and several requests show identical user-agent fingerprints. Details attached to this thread (suspicious_accounts_20260109.txt).

Summary:
- 42 grants of $250 trial credits auto-issued (self-serve)
- 31 accounts created within 30 minutes
- Shared IP cluster and UA fingerprints
- Several accounts linked to the same company name (BrightChat) but using many free email providers and plus-addressing

Action suggested: please triage for potential abuse. We recommend pausing any further auto-grants to the BrightChat domain and consider revoking credits pending manual verification.

Automated Fraud Ops
Redwood Inference Abuse Detection
From: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood-inference.com, dev_patel@redwood-inference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: [Automated] High-volume promo credit issuance — cluster detected

Forwarding automated alert — looks like a BrightChat wave. I dug into HubSpot and these are mostly new contacts created through PLG signups in the last 48h (HC-4521). A few notes: one signup used a brightchat.ai address but the majority are free-email variants with +tagging.

Can Security/Infra confirm whether these were legitimate QA/internal signups from BrightChat, or a coordinated attempt to drain credits? My ask:
- Aditya: can you check the account creation logs + device fingerprints and confirm linkages between accounts?
- Dev: if we need to revoke credits, please prepare revocation artifacts and a short rollback plan (impact, timing, notice to customer).

If this is BrightChat QA, we should make an exception but validate through corporate email or an attestation. I do not want to auto-reinstate credits without a signed consent.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood-inference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, dev_patel@redwood-inference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: [Automated] High-volume promo credit issuance — cluster detected

Marissa — quick triage done (logs attached). Findings:
- 38 of the 42 accounts share the same pair of source IPs: 34.108.2.45 and 34.108.2.78, both seen in a 17m window.
- 29 accounts use Gmail with +aliases (+qa, +test, +1 patterns).
- Device fingerprinting shows identical viewport and accept-language across 24 accounts (strong bot signal).
- 3 accounts show a brightchat.ai corporate address but the TM (time-to-match) for company name on profile is ~8s — likely copy/paste via script.

Recommendation: immediate temporary revocation of the promo credits and suspend auto-grant for brightchat.ai until we get verification. Keep logs and take CSV export (revocation_log_20260109.csv). We should also rate-limit self-serve grant flows for new accounts coming from those IP ranges.

I can pull the full audit trail and add to an internal incident (INC-20260109-ABUSE). Let me know when Dev revokes so I can tag logs for forensics.

— Aditya
From: dev_patel@redwood-inference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, aditya_rao@redwood-inference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: [Automated] High-volume promo credit issuance — cluster detected

Marissa / Aditya — completed the revocation for the 42 accounts. Actions taken:
- Revoked $250 promo credits from all flagged accounts at 10:08 PST (see revocation_log_20260109.csv).
- Marked accounts for manual review and rate-limited new self-serve grants from the two IPs in question.
- Exported suspected accounts to suspicious_accounts_20260109.txt and uploaded to the internal drive.

Impact: any legitimate users from BrightChat will lose the trial credit and will need manual reapproval.

If Sales wants to re-issue credits for verified corporate accounts, we require a signed attestation or a DocuSign approval from an authorized BrightChat rep. I can prepare a short remediation playbook for CS.

- Dev
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@brightchat.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Cc: ops@brightchat.ai, billing@brightchat.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Suspicious batch issuance of trial credits — BrightChat accounts flagged

Hi Marissa — thanks for flagging and sorry for the trouble. Some context: we were running an internal QA sweep and several engineers used personal emails with +tags to spin up quick test accounts across browsers/regions. That said, we should have pre-notified you.

What we can provide immediately:
- A signed attestation from our Head of Ops confirming these are internal QA accounts (I can get that signed today).
- A CSV of employee emails and a list of IP ranges used for the sweep.

Please confirm what format you need for the attestation and whether a DocuSign envelope is acceptable. We want to restore any legitimate credits.

— Liam
